Celina paid 13 and a half million dollars for the old grain silos by downtown, and now we know what it wants to build there.

Celina's Economic Development Corporation showed a draft master plan Sept. 28 for the Willock Tract, about 32 acres of old grain silos near downtown. It bought the land in 2024 for $13.5 million from a half-cent sales tax.

The draft keeps the silos and adds a brewery and beer garden, food halls, live-music restaurants along Doe Branch Creek, a hotel with a conference center, and retail and offices along Oklahoma Drive. City council sees it Oct. 13. Rezoning and tenants come after that.

Celina's median sale over the last 12 months was $512,250, down 7.6%.

Would you walk here from the square?

Colleyville raised its city property tax rate 13 percent, and the new budget year started October 1st.

Colleyville City Council approved a $98.3 million budget and a city tax rate of 35.248 cents per $100 of value, up from 31.19 cents, a 13% increase. The fiscal year started Oct. 1. The city says the owner of an average $678,000 home will pay about $283 more a year in city tax. Water and wastewater base charges also rose $5.07 a month.

The city's finance director said overall property values fell 3% this year, so the rate had to rise to collect the same revenue. Over the last 12 months, Colleyville's median sale price was $1,015,000, up 3.5%. Appraised values and sale prices measure different things.

McKinney's planning commission voted unanimously to put townhomes on 27 acres of North Custer Road, north of 380, and the city council takes the final vote October 20th.

McKinney's Planning and Zoning Commission unanimously recommended annexing and zoning nearly 32 acres on North Custer Road, north of US 380: about 27 acres for townhomes and about 5 acres of commercial facing Custer. City council votes Oct. 20.

The proposed zoning is TR1.8, McKinney's high-density townhome district, which allows up to 24 units per acre. That's a maximum, and the final plan can come in lower. The city received no letters of support or opposition.

McKinney's median sale over the last 12 months was $492,756, up 5.1%.

Prosper just approved 12 shopping and restaurant buildings at Frontier Parkway and the Dallas Parkway, after its planning commission sent the plan back eight times.

Prosper approved Frontier Gateway, 12 retail, restaurant and office buildings on the southwest corner of Frontier Parkway and Dallas Parkway, along the future Dallas North Tollway. The planning commission tabled it eight times over nine months before passing it 6-0 on Aug. 18. Council approved the development agreement Sept. 22.

What changed: a big-box store became two mixed-use buildings, a pharmacy on the main corner became more restaurants and retail, and the center pond got wider with walking trails. It'll be built in two phases, north half first.

Prosper's median sale over the last 12 months was $840,025.

What would you want on that corner?
